beats.beat: The company wins contracts through a competitive tender process. Clients float a tender, a pre-bid meeting is held, contractors bid, and the lowest quote typically wins. The contractor then deposits a performance guarantee.

Its infrastructure work covers railways (platforms, station buildings, gauge conversion, track laying), bridges (various types including beam, cantilever, arch, suspension, cable-stayed, and truss), and roadways (bituminous and concrete roads). It also operates a ready-mix concrete (RMC) plant at Kashimira, Thane.

Major clients include the Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai (MCGM), Western Railway, Central Railway, Mumbai Railway Vikas Corporation Ltd (MRVCL), Mumbai Metropolitan Region Development Authority (MMRDA), Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Ltd, and private firms like Sky Way Infrastructure Private Limited.

Western Railway has been a client since 2006 and is a major contributor. As of the filing, Western Railway accounts for 52% of the orders on hand. The company's top customers contributed 57% of total revenue in FY2018.
The company is geographically concentrated in Mumbai and Maharashtra, with a healthy order book but slow pace of government projects cited as a weakness.

beats.beat: Revenue from operations declined from ₹9,021.12 lakhs in FY2015 to ₹6,053.05 lakhs in FY2018, a drop of about 33% over four years.
Profit after tax (PAT) showed wide swings: ₹95.95 lakhs in FY2014, ₹78.36 lakhs in FY2015, ₹32.63 lakhs in FY2016, ₹15.86 lakhs in FY2017, and then a sharp jump to ₹314.66 lakhs in FY2018.
EBITDA (Profit Before Interest, Depreciation and Tax) also fluctuated: ₹784.46 lakhs in FY2014, ₹945.78 lakhs in FY2015, ₹783.31 lakhs in FY2016, ₹676.19 lakhs in FY2017, and ₹928.80 lakhs in FY2018.

Total assets grew from ₹7,062.34 lakhs in FY2014 to ₹8,232.15 lakhs in FY2018. Long-term borrowings declined from ₹586.63 lakhs to ₹133.09 lakhs over the same period, while short-term borrowings increased from ₹3,082.27 lakhs to ₹3,537.35 lakhs.
Key ratios: basic EPS was ₹1.31 for FY2016, ₹0.63 for FY2017, and ₹12.59 for FY2018. Net Asset Value (NAV) per share was ₹28.14 in FY2018.
The company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, though exact figures are not disclosed in the digest. This is flagged as a risk by the company.

beats.beat: The sole promoter is Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 74,95,476 equity shares (90.949% of the pre-issue capital). Other directors hold only 300 shares each. Key management personnel include CFO Anchal Pachori (aged 28, CA) and Company Secretary Mohit Soni (aged 26, ACS).

Related-party transactions in FY2018 include loans taken from KMP/Board of Directors (₹68.4 lakhs), director remuneration (₹57.7 lakhs), and outstanding payables to related parties (₹324.3 lakhs). The company acknowledges it has entered into related-party transactions in the past and may continue to do so.

Two companies promoted by the promoter – Al-Noor Chickens Private Limited and A B Magma Automobiles Private Limited – were struck off by the Registrar of Companies in March 2016 due to non-operation. The company has issued equity shares in the last 12 months at a price that may be lower than the issue price.

No criminal cases have been filed against directors, and none are on the RBI list of willful defaulters. However, the company and its directors are involved in pending litigation, the outcome of which could be adverse.

beats.beat: The infrastructure sector (power, bridges, dams, roads, urban infrastructure) contributes about 8% to India's GDP at constant prices. The market is highly fragmented and working capital intensive.

India required investment worth ₹50 trillion (US$777.73 billion) in infrastructure by 2022 for sustainable development. Government flagship programs like Smart Cities Mission, AMRUT, Make in India, and Power for All are key demand drivers.

The logistics sector is expected to grow at a CAGR of 10.5% from US$160 billion in 2017 to US$215 billion by 2020. FDI in construction development from April 2000 to December 2017 stood at US$24.67 billion.
Competition is from both organized and unorganized players. The company identifies slow pace of government projects, working capital crunch, and changes in government policies as headwinds.

beats.beat: A B Infrabuild Limited operates in two segments: creation of infrastructure (railways, bridges, roads) and operating a ready-mix concrete plant. Most of its revenue comes from government and PSU contracts, especially Indian Railways.
The company is entirely controlled by promoter Amit Bholanath Mishra, who holds 90.949% of the pre-issue equity.
It is raising funds through a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each, with the price to be determined. The main object is to meet working capital requirements of ₹1,130 lakhs.

intro.purpose: Orient the reader: A B Infrabuild is a Mumbai-based infrastructure construction and ready-mix concrete company, heavily reliant on government clients, planning an SME IPO to raise working capital.

beats.beat: The issue is a fresh issue of 44,28,000 equity shares of ₹10 each. The price band is not yet disclosed; it will be determined later. There is no offer for sale component.
The lead manager to the issue is Mark Corporate Advisors Private Limited. The registrar is Bigshare Services Private Limited.

The primary object is to meet working capital requirements, with ₹1,130 lakhs allocated. A portion is kept for general corporate purposes, the amount of which is not disclosed. The company has not appointed an independent agency for project appraisal or a monitoring agency.

beats.beat: Customer concentration: Western Railway (Indian Railways) contributed 52% of orders on hand and the top customers 57% of FY2018 revenue. Loss of Indian Railways as a customer would cause a significant revenue drop.

Tender-dependent revenue: the company's revenues depend on winning bids from government and PSU clients. If bids are not accepted or are awarded at lower values, financial condition could be materially affected.
Negative cash flows: the company has experienced negative cash flows in recent years, which could impair its ability to meet obligations or fund operations.
Unsecured loans repayable on demand: as of March 31, 2018, the company had ₹405.02 lakhs in unsecured loans that are repayable on demand. A sudden repayment demand could strain liquidity.

Promoter-related red flags: two companies promoted by the promoter were struck off for non-operation, and the company has issued shares below the IPO price in the last 12 months. These raise governance concerns.
